title: Best time to visit Darjeeling, month by month
meta_description: When to go to Darjeeling: clear Kangchenjunga views Oct–Dec, flowers and first flush Mar–Apr, monsoon Jun–Sep. Temperatures, crowds and prices month by month.
summary: For mountain views, go from mid-October to mid-December, or in clear, cold January and February. For flowers, first-flush tea and mild days, go in March and April. May and June are busiest and hazier; June to September brings heavy rain, cloud and landslides but the lowest prices. Avoid the Puja and summer-holiday peaks if you can.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Darjeeling has four seasons that matter to a traveller. Autumn, from October to early December, has the clearest skies, dry roads and the best chance of seeing Kangchenjunga from Chowrasta at dawn. Winter, December to February, is cold but often even clearer, and rooms are cheap. Spring, March to May, is mild and green, with rhododendrons and magnolias in flower and the first-flush tea harvest, but haze builds by late April. The monsoon, June to September, is wet, misty and quiet.

Our favourite windows are the second half of October before the Puja holidays end, the last two weeks of November, and the first half of March. Each gives you good weather, open roads and fair hotel rates. If you can only come in the school holidays, book early and plan your sightseeing for early mornings, when the views are clearest and the roads emptiest.

sections.heading: Spring: March to May
paras: Spring is when the hills are at their most colourful. Magnolias and cherry flower on the slopes in March, and rhododendrons bloom from April into May, especially on the Singalila ridge towards Sandakphu. Tea gardens are busy with the first-flush harvest from late February to April, the best time to see plucking and taste the year's freshest tea. Days are pleasant, around 10–18 °C in April, and nights still need a jacket.

The catch is haze. By mid-April, dust and smoke from the plains and rising heat often hide Kangchenjunga by 8 or 9 am. Get out early: views at dawn are still common in March and April. From May, school holidays across India fill hotels, Tiger Hill jams with cars and rates peak. If you must come in May, book early, avoid weekends at the big sights and keep afternoons for tea rooms and walks.

sections.heading: Monsoon: June to September
paras: The monsoon usually reaches the hills in the first half of June and stays into late September. Darjeeling gets most of its rain, roughly 2,500–3,000 mm a year in total, in these four months, with July and August the wettest. Cloud and mist sit on the ridge for days; you may not see the mountains at all. Landslides close stretches of road, especially on the lower routes towards Siliguri and Kalimpong, and sometimes stop the toy train.

There are reasons to come. Hotels cut rates by 30–50 percent, the hills are intensely green, the tea gardens are still plucking, and the town belongs to its residents. Plan with care: keep a spare day before any flight or train, travel in daylight, carry a good rain jacket and leech socks for walks, and check current status before you travel. Singalila National Park, with the Sandakphu trek, closes to trekkers from mid-June to mid-September, and the Dooars parks below close in the same months.

sections.heading: Autumn: October and November
paras: Autumn is the classic Darjeeling season. The monsoon washes the air clean, and from early October the mornings turn clear, with Kangchenjunga sharp against a blue sky. Days are around 11–18 °C in October and cooler in November. This is the best time for Tiger Hill, the Sandakphu trek and photography, and the autumn-flush tea comes in.

It is also festival time. Dashain, the biggest festival of the Nepali-speaking community, falls in late September or October; Durga Puja brings huge numbers of visitors from Kolkata and Bangladesh in the same weeks; and Tihar follows around Diwali, with lamps, garlands and sel roti in every home. Hotels and the toy train sell out in the Puja weeks. The second half of November, after the holidays, is calmer and cheaper, with the same clear skies.

Height changes everything. Kurseong, at 1,458 m, and Mirik, at about 1,495 m, stay a few degrees warmer than Darjeeling and are pleasant even in January, while Tiger Hill at 2,567 m is colder and windier at dawn. Sandakphu at 3,636 m is a different climate altogether: freezing nights for much of the year and snow in winter. Pack for the highest place on your plan, not the average.

sections.heading: Winter: December to February
paras: Winter is cold, dry and often the clearest time of year. Daytime highs are about 4–11 °C and nights fall close to freezing, colder at Tiger Hill and far below zero at Sandakphu. Many hotels have heaters or electric blankets, but older buildings can be chilly; ask before booking. Snow in Darjeeling town is rare and falls on only a few days in some winters, usually in January or February.

Prices fall sharply in January and February, and the views can be superb. The Ghum Festival of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway runs in late November and early December, Christmas is warmly celebrated in the town's churches and schools, and Losar, the Tibetan new year, falls in February or March, with dances at the monasteries of Ghum and Darjeeling. Pack thermals, a down jacket, gloves and a woollen cap.

sections.heading: Festivals and events through the year
paras: Festivals add colour to a trip and also move hotel prices, so it helps to know when they fall. Most hill festivals follow the lunar calendar, which means their dates shift by a few weeks from year to year. Confirm the exact days before you book, and check current status before you travel for any public event.

Remember that the big festivals are family time for local people. Some shops and eateries close for a day or two, shared jeeps run less often, and hotel staff may be on leave. That rarely spoils a trip, and seeing a town celebrate is often a highlight, but keep plans flexible in those weeks.
list: Losar, the Tibetan new year, in February or March: masked dances and prayers at Ghum's Yiga Choeling and Darjeeling's monasteries.
Saga Dawa and Buddha Jayanti in May or June: processions with holy texts through Darjeeling town on the full moon.
Dashain in late September or October: ten days ending on Vijaya Dashami, when elders give tika and blessings; many businesses close for a few days.
Tihar around Diwali in October or November: five days of lamps, marigold garlands, sel roti and the songs of deusi-bhailo groups going house to house.
Ghum Festival of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway in late November and early December: special steam runs, exhibitions and local food.
Christmas in December: carols and midnight services in the town's old churches and schools.

sections.heading: Choosing by what you want
paras: Different travellers want different things from Darjeeling. Here is how we match the month to the purpose.
list: Kangchenjunga views and photography: mid-October to February, with November and December the most reliable.
Sandakphu trek: October to November for views, April to May for rhododendrons; the park closes mid-June to mid-September.
Tea gardens: late March to June for first and second flush; October to November for autumn flush. Factories rest in winter.
Toy train: any month outside the heaviest monsoon weeks; book well ahead for October, May and June.
Lowest prices: July, August, January and February.
Families with school holidays: book by February for May and June, and by July for the Puja weeks.
Honeymoons: late November to early December, or March, for clear skies and fewer crowds.

faqs.q: Which is the best month to visit Darjeeling
faqs.a: November is our pick: clear skies, dry roads, crisp days around 7–15 °C and, after the Puja weeks, fewer crowds. October, December and March are close behind. For flowers and first-flush tea, choose late March or April. For the lowest prices with good views, choose January or February and pack for the cold.

faqs.q: Can we see Kangchenjunga from Darjeeling in May
faqs.a: Sometimes, early in the morning. By May, haze and pre-monsoon cloud often hide the mountains after about 8 am, and some days you see nothing. Your best chance is dawn from Chowrasta, Observatory Hill or Tiger Hill. For reliable views, travel between mid-October and February instead.

Rarely in the town itself. Darjeeling gets light snow on a few days in some winters, usually in January or February, and none at all in others. Tiger Hill gets snow a little more often, and Sandakphu is regularly snowbound from December to March. For dependable snow, families usually go to Tsomgo Lake near Gangtok.

faqs.q: Is it safe to visit Darjeeling in the monsoon
faqs.a: Yes, with care. The town itself is safe, but heavy rain causes landslides that close roads and sometimes stop the toy train, especially in July and August. Travel in daylight, keep a spare day before flights or trains, and follow local news. Check current status before you travel, and expect few mountain views.

faqs.q: How cold is Darjeeling in December
faqs.a: Daytime temperatures are about 4–11 °C, and nights fall close to 0 °C. Tiger Hill at dawn is colder, often below freezing with wind. Bring thermals, a down or heavy fleece jacket, gloves, a woollen cap and warm socks. Hotels in older buildings can be chilly, so ask about heaters before you book.

From mid-April to mid-June, during school summer holidays, and in the Durga Puja to Diwali weeks of October and November. The Christmas to New Year week is also busy. Expect higher hotel rates, sold-out toy-train seats and traffic jams at Tiger Hill and on the road from Siliguri at these times.

Yes. January and February are among the cheapest months, with many hotels discounting 20–40 percent, and skies are often very clear. Late December is the exception, as Christmas and New Year bring crowds. The monsoon months of July and August are cheaper still, but with rain and few views.

faqs.q: When is the first flush tea season
faqs.a: From late February to April, after the bushes rest through winter. This is the best time to see plucking in the gardens and to taste and buy the year's freshest tea. Second flush follows in May and June, and the autumn flush in October and November. Factories rest from December to February.

faqs.q: What should I pack for Darjeeling in April
faqs.a: Light layers for days around 10–18 °C, a warm sweater or fleece for evenings, a light down jacket for Tiger Hill at dawn, a compact umbrella or rain shell for pre-monsoon showers, sunscreen and walking shoes with grip. April evenings can drop below 10 °C, so do not pack only summer clothes.
